Analyze subgroup for GLM outcomes

Source: R/summary_utility_functions.R
analyze_subgroup_glm.Rd

GLM counterpart to analyze_subgroup. Computes per-arm outcome rates, sample sizes, and the treatment effect estimate (RD, OR, etc.) using the estimator closure.

Usage

analyze_subgroup_glm(
  df_sub,
  outcome.name,
  treat.name,
  subgroup_name,
  effect_a = NA,
  estimator_fn = NULL,
  effect_measure = "RD",
  outcome_type = "binary",
  N,
  digits = 4
)

Arguments

df_sub

Data frame for the subgroup.

outcome.name

Character. Name of outcome variable.

treat.name

Character. Name of treatment variable.

subgroup_name

Character. Label for this subgroup.

effect_a

Character. Adjusted effect estimate string (optional).

estimator_fn

Closure from make_effect_estimator(), or NULL.

effect_measure

Character. Effect measure label (e.g., "RD", "OR").

outcome_type

Character. One of "binary", "continuous", or "count". Controls formatting: binary displays per-arm means as percentages ("Rate"); continuous and count display raw means ("Mean"). Default "binary".

N

Integer. Total sample size (for percentage calculation).

digits

Integer. Number of decimal places for arm-mean / Diff / effect-estimate / CI numeric formatting. Default 4 to provide headroom for downstream display reformatting (e.g., via summarize_bootstrap_results(digits = ...), which can round down but cannot recover precision lost at construction). Note this does not affect the count-with-percent-of-total formatting in the n and n1 columns, which remain at 1 decimal.

Value

One-row data frame of formatted subgroup results. Column names are placeholders (Subgroup, n, n1, rate0, rate1, Diff, effect, optionally effect_a) and are overwritten by the calling function (SG_tab_estimates_glm) with the user-facing labels (e.g., "Rate(C)" vs "Mean(C)", the effect-measure header). Returning a data frame – rather than a named character vector via c(...) – ensures type stability across the ITT and subgroup call paths and prevents downstream rendering failures in consumers that go through as.data.frame() (e.g., gt).
